subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the centre, eccentricity, foci, length of the latus rectum and equations of the directrices of the hyperbola 16y² − 9x² = 144.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.66 — SAQ chapter 9 Hyperbola, answer 78.2, the second of the printed twin pair 78.1/78.2. insider_note: Whenever the y² term is positive, swap every a ↔ b role from the familiar x²/a² − y²/b² formulas — eccentricity, foci, directrices and latus rectum all use b in place of a.

steps.label: Write in standard form
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own — every result below reads a and b off this line, but note which axis is transverse.
steps.memory_tip: The transverse axis is decided by which term is POSITIVE, not by which denominator is bigger.
lines: so the transverse axis is the y-axis.
steps.why: The transverse axis is decided by which squared term is POSITIVE, not by which of a² and b² is larger — here y² is positive even though b² = 9 is smaller than a² = 16, so the foci and vertices lie on the y-axis.
common_mistakes: Assuming the transverse axis lies along the axis with the larger denominator, as for an ellipse's major axis — a hyperbola's transverse axis is decided by the SIGN, not the size.
Mislabeling a² and b²: a² always stays attached to the x² denominator, b² to the y² denominator, whichever axis is transverse.

steps.label: Eccentricity
steps.margin_note: First mark. The transverse axis is y, so the eccentricity formula divides by b, not a.
steps.memory_tip: y² positive ⇒ read every formula with a and b swapped from the usual x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 case.
steps.why: When the transverse axis is the y-axis, the eccentricity formula uses b (the term on the transverse axis) in the denominator, not a.
common_mistakes: Dividing by a instead of b — here the transverse axis is y, so b is the axis length that belongs in the denominator.
Writing √25 as 25 instead of simplifying the root to 5.

steps.label: Foci
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The foci lie above and below the centre, not to its sides.
steps.why: The foci lie on the transverse axis — here the y-axis — at distance be from the centre on each side.
common_mistakes: Placing the foci on the x-axis out of habit.
Using ae instead of be for the distance, since here it is b, not a, that carries the transverse-axis role.

steps.label: Equations of the directrices
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Two horizontal lines, one above and one below the centre.
steps.memory_tip: y² positive ⇒ directrices are y = ±b/e, horizontal lines, not vertical.
steps.why: Each directrix is the horizontal line y = b/e or y = −b/e — the reciprocal relation of the focus formula y = ±be.
common_mistakes: Writing the directrix as a vertical line instead of horizontal — the transverse axis here is y, so the directrices are horizontal lines.
Confusing y = b/e with the focus formula y = be.

steps.label: Length of the latus rectum
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The formula also swaps roles here.
steps.memory_tip: y² positive ⇒ latus rectum is 2a²/b, not 2b²/a.
lines: Length of the latus rectum = 2a² / b
steps.why: The latus rectum formula swaps roles here too — it uses 2a²/b, not 2b²/a, because b is now the transverse-axis length.
common_mistakes: Reusing 2b²/a from the horizontal case without swapping a and b.
Forgetting to double a² before dividing by b.
